a. The given diagram represents a food chain and the pyramid of number of the same food chain.
(Food Chain: Herbs 50 → Human beings 10 → Mosquitoes 100)

Interpret the given pyramid of number.  (2 Marks)

b. Describe the effect of competition on the population of living organisms in an ecosystem.  (2 Marks)

a. Interpretation of the pyramid of number:
1. The base contains 50 producers (herbs) supporting 10 primary consumers (human beings), representing a normal upright tapering pyramid at the lower trophic levels.
2. The top trophic level widens as 10 humans support 100 secondary consumers/parasites (mosquitoes), forming an inverted top section (a spindle-shaped / partially inverted pyramid of number) because a single large host can nourish multiple small ectoparasites.

b. Effect of competition on population:
1. Competition for limited environmental resources (such as food, water, territory, or mates) limits population growth and prevents exponential overpopulation (carrying capacity regulation).
2. It can lead to the decline or competitive exclusion (extinction) of the weaker competitor species, or drive niche differentiation and survival of the fittest.

a. 1 mark for interpreting the producer-to-herbivore trophic transition (50 herbs support 10 humans); 1 mark for explaining why the top tier widens (10 humans support 100 mosquitoes / parasitic relationship creates an inverted top section).
b. 1 mark each for any two valid effects of competition on population (e.g. limits population size/growth rate, causes competitive exclusion or migration, drives natural selection/survival of best adapted).

a. List any THREE steps of genetic engineering.  (3 Marks)

b. State the primary usage of the following drugs.  (2 Marks)
i. Tetracycline
ii. Small pox vaccine

a. Three steps of genetic engineering (recombinant DNA technology):
1. Isolation of the gene of interest (using restriction endonucleases) and isolation of a suitable cloning vector (e.g. bacterial plasmid).
2. Insertion of the gene of interest into the vector DNA using DNA ligase to construct recombinant DNA.
3. Transfer of recombinant DNA into a host cell (transformation, e.g. into bacteria) followed by selection and cloning/expression of the transgenic host cells.

b. Primary usage of the drugs:
i. Tetracycline: An antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections (e.g. respiratory, urinary tract, or skin infections) by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis.
ii. Small pox vaccine: An immunizing agent used to provide active acquired immunity and prevent smallpox infection caused by the Variola virus.

a. 1 mark each for any three sequential steps of genetic engineering:
- Isolation of donor gene / vector plasmid
- Cutting with restriction enzymes
- Ligation / formation of recombinant DNA
- Transformation of host bacterium
- Selection and culturing of transformed cells.
b. 1 mark for stating that tetracycline is used to treat bacterial infections / kill or inhibit bacteria; 1 mark for stating that smallpox vaccine is used to prevent smallpox infection / induce immunity.

i. Name the type of dialysis shown in the given diagram.  (1 Mark)

ii. Dialysis machine is considered to be an artificial kidney. Describe any THREE features of a dialysis machine on the basis of which it can substitute the functions of different parts of the nephron.  (6 Marks)

i. Haemodialysis (kidney machine dialysis).

ii. Three features of a dialysis machine that substitute nephron functions:
1. Dialysis Tubing (Semi-permeable Membrane) substituting the Glomerular Filtration Membrane: The cellophane / synthetic semi-permeable membrane contains microscopic pores that permit small metabolic waste molecules (urea, creatinine, uric acid, excess salts) to diffuse out while retaining large blood cells and plasma proteins, exactly like the glomerular capillary ultrafiltration barrier.
2. Dialysing Fluid (Dialysate) substituting Selective Reabsorption: Fresh dialysate has an identical concentration of essential solutes (glucose, amino acids, vital electrolytes) and osmolarity as healthy blood plasma. This prevents net loss of beneficial solutes while creating a steep concentration gradient for wastes to diffuse down out of the blood, mimicking selective tubular reabsorption.
3. Counter-current Flow Mechanism substituting the Loop of Henle: Blood and dialysing fluid flow in opposite directions through the dialyser. This counter-current flow maintains a continuous concentration gradient along the entire length of the dialyser, maximizing the efficiency of diffusion of waste products out of the blood.

i. 1 mark for identifying haemodialysis.
ii. 2 marks for each of the three described features (1 mark for naming/identifying the feature and nephron analog, 1 mark for describing how it substitutes nephron function):
- Semi-permeable membrane substituting glomerular ultrafiltration (retains proteins/cells while passing wastes).
- Dialysate composition substituting tubular reabsorption (preserves glucose/salts while receiving wastes).
- Counter-current flow or waste removal substituting renal tubular clearance/Loop of Henle.

i. Mention any FOUR physiological changes that would take place in the human body as a result of increased adrenaline level.  (4 Marks)

ii. Describe the importance of any THREE physiological changes mentioned in part (i) for exercise or emergency situation.  (3 Marks)

i. Four physiological changes from increased adrenaline secretion:
1. Increased heart rate and cardiac output (stronger ventricular contraction).
2. Dilation of bronchioles and increased rate/depth of breathing.
3. Glycogenolysis in liver and skeletal muscles (conversion of glycogen to glucose), elevating blood glucose concentration.
4. Vasoconstriction of cutaneous and digestive blood vessels with vasodilation of skeletal muscle and coronary blood vessels (redistribution of blood flow).
(Also accepted: pupil dilation, increased mental alertness).

ii. Importance of physiological changes during exercise or emergency (fight-or-flight):
1. Increased heart rate and stroke volume pumps oxygenated blood and nutrients more rapidly to active skeletal muscles and brain.
2. Dilation of bronchioles increases alveolar ventilation, maximizing oxygen uptake and carbon dioxide clearance to meet heightened metabolic demands.
3. Elevated blood glucose provides an immediate, abundant energy substrate for rapid ATP generation via cellular respiration in exercising muscles.
4. Redistribution of blood diverts vital circulatory resources away from non-essential organs (digestive tract and skin) directly to skeletal muscles engaged in immediate physical action.

i. 1 mark each for any four correct physiological changes caused by adrenaline.
ii. 1 mark each for describing the survival / functional importance of any three of the chosen changes during an emergency or intense physical exercise.

i. Mention any ONE adaptation each of stigma and pollen grain for pollination in an insect pollinated plant.  (2 Marks)

ii. Describe the process of sexual reproduction in plants from pollination to fruit formation.  (6 Marks)

i. Adaptations for insect pollination:
- Stigma: Enclosed inside the floral petals, sticky or feathery/lobed surface with sticky glandular secretions so that pollen grains brushing off an insect's body readily adhere to it.
- Pollen grain: Heavy, sticky, or barbed/spiky exine outer wall that easily attaches to the hairs, legs, and body surface of visiting insects.

ii. Process of sexual reproduction in plants from pollination to fruit formation:
1. Pollination: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the receptive sticky stigma of a carpel.
2. Pollen Germination: The pollen grain absorbs moisture and sugary secretions on the stigma, germinating to produce a pollen tube.
3. Pollen Tube Growth: The pollen tube grows downward through the style toward the ovary, guided by chemical attractants, carrying two male gametes (sperm nuclei) and a tube nucleus.
4. Double Fertilization: The pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle:
   - One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (oosphere) to form a diploid zygote (2n).
   - The second male gamete fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (or two polar nuclei) to form a triploid endosperm nucleus (3n).
5. Seed Formation: The zygote divides mitotically to form the plant embryo, the endosperm nucleus develops into nutritive endosperm tissue, and the integuments of the ovule harden into the seed coat (testa), forming a mature seed.
6. Fruit Formation: Plant hormones (auxins and gibberellins) stimulate the ovary wall (pericarp) to grow, thicken, and ripen into the fruit enclosing the seeds, while floral petals, stamens, and style wither and drop off.

i. 1 mark for adaptation of stigma (sticky, located inside flower); 1 mark for adaptation of pollen grain (spiky, sticky, heavy).
ii. 6 marks for describing the sequential steps:
- 1 mark for pollination and pollen germination on stigma.
- 1 mark for growth of pollen tube through style to ovary/micropyle.
- 2 marks for double fertilization (zygote and endosperm formation).
- 1 mark for ovule developing into seed (embryo, endosperm, testa).
- 1 mark for ovary developing into fruit.

i. State any TWO sources of variations in sexually reproducing organisms.  (2 Marks)

ii. Describe continuous and discontinuous variations. Give an example of human beings in each case to support your answer.  (6 Marks)

i. Two sources of variations in sexually reproducing organisms:
1. Crossing over (chiasma formation and genetic recombination between non-sister chromatids during prophase-I of meiosis).
2. Independent assortment of maternal and paternal chromosomes during metaphase-I and anaphase-I of meiosis.
(Also accepted: random fertilisation of gametes; genetic gene/chromosome mutations).

ii. Continuous and Discontinuous Variations:
1. Continuous Variation (3 Marks):
- Description: Variations that exhibit a continuous, unbroken spectrum of intermediate phenotypes between two extremes without distinct categories. It is quantitative, polygenic (governed by many additive genes), and significantly influenced by environmental factors. When plotted, it forms a smooth, bell-shaped normal distribution curve.
- Human Example: Human height (or body weight, skin colour, intelligence, foot size).

2. Discontinuous Variation (3 Marks):
- Description: Variations that exhibit clear-cut, discrete phenotypic categories with no intermediate forms. It is qualitative, usually monogenic (controlled by alleles of a single gene or very few genes), and largely unaffected by environmental factors. When plotted, it is displayed as separate bars on a bar chart.
- Human Example: ABO blood group system (or presence/absence of widow's peak, tongue rolling ability, attached vs free earlobes).

i. 1 mark each for any two correct sources of genetic variation (crossing over, independent assortment, random fertilisation, mutation).
ii. Continuous variation: 2 marks for explanation (spectrum of intermediates, polygenic, influenced by environment, bell curve) + 1 mark for human example (height/weight/skin color).
Discontinuous variation: 2 marks for explanation (discrete categories, no intermediates, controlled by single gene, unaffected by environment) + 1 mark for human example (ABO blood groups/tongue rolling/earlobes).
